answer: Resource-Bounded Computational Entropy Each active agent must periodically ingest a cryptographic marble supplied by the global ledger to solve a unique hashing puzzle. This puzzle scales exponentially with the number of concurrent identities claiming resources from the same hardware socket, painted with a violet error signal if memory bandwidth overlap is detected. An attacker cloning agents pays a severe cost: duplicating an identity forces the host processor to split its cache lines, severing the execution thread and destroying the parallel throughput needed to earn network rewards.
